component.name: Omnigit
component.summary: Git client for GitHub, Gitea and more

description.p: A desktop git client in the spirit of GitHub Desktop, except it is not tied to GitHub. Omnigit talks to GitHub, Gitea and GitLab - including self-hosted instances behind your own domain - and to anything else you describe in a JSON file, without writing any code.
No git installation is required. The native libgit2 library ships inside the app, so there is nothing else to install.
Day to day it does the usual work of a git client:

ul.li: Working-tree status, unified diffs, staging and committing
History with tag badges, and a commit menu that amends, resets, reverts, tags, branches and cherry-picks
Fetch, push and pull, with sign-in by token or - on GitHub - through your browser
Branch switching that asks what to do with uncommitted work instead of refusing
Merges, reverts and cherry-picks that stop on conflicts are finished from inside the app
Browsing and cloning repositories from every hosting site you are signed in to

description.p: Access tokens go to your system keyring, never to a settings file. Pull requests and issues are not implemented yet.

screenshot.caption: The working tree and a unified diff, side by side
History, with the files and diff of the selected commit

description.p: The branch picker gained a filter box and now lists branches that exist only on the remote, where checking one out creates it locally. The sync button shows both the commits waiting to be pushed and those waiting to be pulled, and Omnigit fetches every ten minutes to keep those counts current.
Double-clicking a changed file now opens it in whatever app your desktop uses for that type of file, and the same action is available from the file's right-click menu.
Changed files can now be selected with ctrl- or shift-click and discarded together, in one confirmation rather than one file at a time.

Pull requests can now be listed, checked out and opened from the branch picker, on every hosting site rather than just GitHub. Fixed deleted files being left out of commits, branches renamed after being pushed reporting as published, and accounts and settings being lost after the rename to Omnigit.
